steps.content: [Lighthouse Top]
The beacon repair is progressing better than expected. The new lens is installed, the circuitry is fixed and dry, and it's all successfully connected to the hand-cranked generator.

The problem is power. You lack Miles's raw strength. Each turn of the crank is like pouring a cup of water into a bottomless pit. You could crank for a lifetime and still not generate enough power for even a faint glow.

Fortunately, the tower has a backup battery array. With the main power system destroyed, it's your only hope. Protocol demands a full circuitry check and a pre-charge test, but time has run out for protocol.
Outside, the humid air grows thick as the water level rises rapidly. After a cursory check for obvious shorts, you start cranking. The power gauge barely twitches from zero.

After nearly half an hour, exhaustion seeps into your muscles. You should have let Ceto handle this brute-force work. But you gave her the more critical job: keeping watch. Just as the thought crosses your mind, Ceto climbs through the window from the tower's top—

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Wait. I saw a surface disturbance. Bearing northeast, 27 degrees.

You squint in the direction she indicates. The waves all look the same to you, a monotonous swell with no distinguishing features. Yet you have no reason to doubt her; this sharpened perception is how she found you in the vast, dark sea.
What do you see?
Ceto frowns thoughtfully, seemingly uncertain herself.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: A fleet. Large. Wave patterns are wrong. Probably interference from multiple ship hulls.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Your friends... this DisCity team coming to rescue you... how many ships do they have?
Command-class. Three capital ships, ten escorts.
Your eyes meet. The same conclusion hangs unspoken between you: this could be the rescue team from DisCity coming for you.
After a moment's pause, you tighten the tool belt and grip the generator handle once more.
Whatever the signal means, this lighthouse is this desolate island's only possible link to the outside world.
The strength from the monster meat fuels you now. You plant your feet and crank the handle with everything you have.

After relentless effort, the charge meter finally creeps from 0% to 1%. You throw open the controller panel and manually override the signal, switching it from Ceto's preset frequency—"Abandon Lighthouse"—to a desperate, repeating "SOS."

The storm redoubles its fury. Wind screams around the lighthouse, and rain lashes the platform, making the footing treacherous. On the distant shore, several monsters breach the boundary. Drawn by the mechanical noise, they begin converging on the lighthouse.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Two disturbances in one day. The Black Tide's retaliation will be severe. That fleet can't approach in the storm that's coming, even if they see a signal.
We still need to let them know we're here. Waiting to die isn't my style. The worse it gets, the tighter we hold onto any chance we get. Like I said before—
Someone is waiting for me.
You bow your head and keep working. Ceto stares at your back, her pessimistic retort dying unspoken.
The remaining glass panes rattle violently in their frames, threatening to shatter. Wind and rain whip sideways into the lighthouse, slicking the crank handle and making it difficult to grip.
Ceto was right—tonight's storm is worse than anything that came before.

The platform shudders violently beneath your feet. You grit your teeth, driving the handle down again and again. Your muscles scream in protest, your joints going numb, but the meter's crawl upward is agonizingly slow.
Just as you're about to be thrown off balance, a solid weight braces against your back, steadying you against the gale.
It's Ceto.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The light's too weak. They'll never see it. We need full power. No distractions.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The storm and the contamination... leave those to me.
You glance back and see that Ceto has fastened the dog tags you recovered for her to her belt.
There once were all the prayers For our loved ones, keeping the light Here comes every victory
Ceto draws her Rancor and takes a defensive position at your back.

Fragments of the weapon slither up her sword arm, adhering to her skin like a living, parasitic entity. She doesn't resist, allowing the razor-sharp shards to burrow into her flesh until they solidify just below her elbow.
Her irises ignite with a crimson glow, pupils contracting to predatory pinpoints—the unmistakable sign she is trading her sanity to the Rancor for power.
For hope, for dawn, for every soul!
